source_title: Sir Patrick Stewart Was One of Only 95 Actors in the World to Have Official Knighthood - People.com

Sir Patrick Stewart was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010 for his contributions to drama
The Star Trek actor was one of only 95 actors in the world to have an official knighthood
Stewart died on Wednesday, Oct. 28, at age 86
Sir Patrick Stewart ’s legacy was marked by various achievements, including being knighted.
The English actor, who died on Wednesday, Oct. 28, at age 86 , was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II at Buckingham Palace in 2010 for his contributions to drama. Stewart — whose decades-long career spanned the big screen and the stage — said he was “very proud” to receive the accolade, according to The Guardian .
“The theatre is and has always been my great joy,” he said. “The theatre is and has always been my great joy. In particular, the past six years have given me acting opportunities that at one time I could not have imagined possible.”
Receiving a knighthood or damehood from a member of the royal family is one of the highest honors a British native can get. A knight or dame title is awarded to “those who have made a significant contribution to their field, usually on a national level,” according to The Royal Family website .
During his January 2015 appearance on Conan , Stewart said receiving knighthood was a “big deal” for him.
“It was totally unexpected,” the Star Trek actor said. “And it almost didn’t happen because it came, the invitation to accept or not this honor, came in a brown envelope, and it was put into a plastic shopping bag with a whole lot of other mail. When I arrived at my destination that weekend, I put it in the closet and found it 10 days later.”
After he found the letter, Stewart said he read it three times because he couldn’t believe he’d be considered for such an esteemed award. “Surely, it’s addressed to the wrong person,” he joked. “They meant the other Patrick Stewart, not me.”
“It was an extraordinary honor. I was thrilled to accept it,” Stewart continued. “Astonished, but proud to be joining the company of long-time dear friends of mine, like Ian McKellen and Derek Jacobi. Terrific actors and good friends.”
Stewart is one of 95 actors in the world to receive official knighthood. Among those who have been knighted are actors Idris Elba , Anthony Hopkins and Daniel Day-Lewis .

On Thursday, Oct. 29, Kelly Bush Novak, a longtime spokesperson for Stewart, announced in a statement that the actor died following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia.
“He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all,” the statement continued. “We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace.”
The legendary actor was best known for portraying Captain Picard in the Star Trek franchise and Professor X in the X-Men films.
Stewart starred as Captain Picard on all seven seasons of Star Trek: The Next Generation , reprising the character in four Star Trek films from 1994 to 2002. He returned to the role in 2020 on the Paramount+ series Star Trek: Picard .
He starred in the X-Men movie franchise for over two decades as Professor Charles Xavier, the mutant telepath. He set the Guinness World Record for the longest Marvel career.
“He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise,” the statement continued.
“His professional accomplishments were humbly matched by his philanthropy and activism on behalf of human rights, survivors of domestic violence, global refugees, veterans’ mental health services, and animal welfare, particularly his cherished foster pitties. He was a Knight, Chancellor, motor sport enthusiast, and lifelong Huddersfield Football fan. He will be remembered for the dignity, compassion and humanity he brought to every role — in his art and life.”
